newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Martinair Tampa stake to lift Latam volumes.
newsitem.headline: Martinair Tampa stake to lift Latam volumes.

text.p: Dutch cargo and charter airline, Martinair Holland bought a stake in Colombian cargo carrier Tampa in a bid to expand its Latin American network, a Martinair spokesman said.
"We have aimed to be stronger in the Latin American market for some years and Tampa has an extensive network in this region," he added.

Martinair said on Wednesday said it was taking a 40 percent stake in Tampa (Transportes Aereos Mercantiles Panamericanos) for an undisclosed sum. The Dutch airline is jointly owned by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV and Nedlloyd
Managers of the Dutch carrier will not be employed at the Colombian carrier and the spokesman stressed that the shareholding is purely a financial stake.
Mexico City, San Jose, Quito, Lima, Santiago de Chile and Sao Paulo are some of the destinations already served by the Dutch carrier.
Privately-owned Tampa, which has a hub in Miami, serves several destinations in Colombia and Venezuela, Bolivia and Peru, as well as elsewhere in Latin America.
This will provide Martinair with several new destinations, he added.
Tampa operates an all-freighter fleet with three Boeing 707s and two Douglas DC-8 aircraft.
Flowers and perishables are a sector that Martinair has been targeting and its Latin America and U.S. representatives work closely with the growers and forwarders.
Martinair has also acquired a ten percent stake in Martin Aviation Group, a general sales agent based in Miami.

The two have worked together for a number of years and this is also part of the ongoing expansion of the Latin American market, said the spokesman. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
